newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close broadly higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close broadly higher.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed broadly higher on Thursday on hopes for declining inflation in 1997, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.09 pct to 104.74
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 to 103.73
Volume, mostly concentrated in the Makam and unlinked bonds, was a moderate 188 million shekels.

"CPI-linked bonds, which rose sharply last month, went through a correction and now they are ready for another rise. The rise of long bonds today indicates that inflation-linked bonds are expected to continue rising with yields falling further below four percent," said Ron Weisberg at I.B.I Investment House.
Yossi Weidelfeld at Eyal Securities added that investors focused on unlinked bonds and Makams.

"Unlinked bonds offer relatively high yields considering the fact that the economy is slowing down. If the inflation will remain under control the Bank of Israel may lower its key lending rate in the future," Weidelfeld said.
Weisberg said the fact that the budget deficit is expected to remain relatively low adds to investors' interest in unlinked bonds.
Israel in March posted a budget surplus of 188 million shekels, which was in line with the Treasury's target.
"Makams offer yields of 14 percent which is very attractive if inflation remains below 10 percent," Weisberg added.

Dollar-linked bonds closed slightly higher in thin trade as the shekel remained almost unchanged against the dollar. In local trading, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3580 shekels against 3.3570 shekels on Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
